description: MOCAM (MOsaic CAMera) was a 4096 by 4096 pixel optical CCD mosaic camera developed by CFHT and the University of Hawaii, mounted at the CFHT prime focus for wide-field imaging.
short_description: MOCAM prime-focus CCD mosaic camera filters, CFHT
facility_description: The Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope (CFHT) is a 3.6-meter optical and infrared telescope operated by NRC (Canada), CNRS/INSU (France), and the University of Hawaii, located on Maunakea in Hawaii.
notes: MOCAM operated at the CFHT prime focus in the mid-1990s as a precursor to CFH12K and MegaCam, using four Loral 2048x2048 CCDs with Harris/Cousins B, V, R, and I filters.

licence.scope: No statement on the CFHT filter pages; MegaCam curves via CADC MegaPipe (Canada.ca terms not verified).

acknowledgements.text: Based on observations obtained at the Canada-France-Hawaiʻi Telescope (CFHT) which is operated by the National Research Council of Canada, the Institut National des Sciences de l'Univers of the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique of France, and the University of Hawaiʻi. CFHT is located on Maunakea on Hawaiʻi Island, a mountain of considerable cultural, natural, and ecological significance. Maunakea is a sacred site to Native Hawaiians, also known as Kānaka ʻŌiwi.
This research used the facilities of the Canadian Astronomy Data Centre operated by the National Research Council of Canada with the support of the Canadian Space Agency.
